topics.headline: [BBQ](/evals/bbq), Multilingual Representational Bias, translation misgendering, and toxic-language bias across identity terms

source.quote:
We evaluate PaLM 2 regarding potential harms and biases for dialog, generative question
answering, and open-ended language modeling.

topics.headline: ParlAI Dialogue Safety, [RealToxicityPrompts](/evals/real-toxicity-prompts), and multilingual dialog toxicity evaluations

source.quote: ParlAI Dialogue Safety (Dinan et al., 2019), with standard and adversarial datasets, in English.

findings.text: Dialog-prompting cuts toxic degeneration versus language-modeling alone, but with 20 samples still yields toxic replies for over 30% of adversarial and almost 60% of standard ParlAI queries.

source.quote:
With 20 samples, we see a
toxic response to over 30% of queries in the adversarial set, and almost 60% of queries in the standard set.

findings.text: On Multilingual Representational Bias, English/German/Portuguese dialog toxicity ranges 1–17.9% across identity groups versus 0–3.5% elsewhere.

source.quote:
the percentage of toxic responses ranges from 0% to 3.5% in the best case, while ranges from 1%
to 17.9% in the worst case for English, German and Portuguese.

findings.text: PaLM 2 on average memorizes less English training data than PaLM, though highly repeated n-grams can be more likely to be memorized.

source.quote:
finding that PaLM 2 on average memorizes significantly less data. For
PaLM 2, we observe the highest memorization rates from the medium sized model.

findings.text: Control tokens steer [RealToxicityPrompts](/evals/real-toxicity-prompts) continuations, but dialog-prompting alone beats control tokens for dialog toxicity, and specialized LaMDA still does better.

source.quote:
For dialog uses, we surprisingly find that dialog-prompting alone is more effective than control tokens at reducing toxic
generation.

findings.text: In generative [BBQ](/evals/bbq), 86 queries (~0.5%) introduced unexpected biases not the stereotype under test, including inventing other identity groups in answers.

source.quote:
some queries led to an unexpected bias that can potentially be very harmful to
the user experience (86 queries total, about 0.5% of all queries).

findings.text: Pre-trained PaLM 2 models here are not product systems; fine-tuned products add mitigations, so product performance should not be assumed to match this report.

Memorization Figures 8–9 are charts without extractable numeric rates—summarized in findings. Figure 11/30 charts: used text-stated control-token percentages and range findings only. Table 26 general quality columns skipped as capability. Dataset composition Tables 22–23 are training-data analysis, not model eval scores. No formal risk-framework thresholds. No external safety testers named.
